title: Chain an audit and a store with Consumer.andThen

blocks.text: `Consumer.andThen` chains consumers: `first.andThen(second)` hands each value to `first`, then to `second`. A bound reference such as `processed::add` is a `Consumer` that stores every value into that one list.
`Order` is a record `(String id, double amount, String customer)`. Write two methods in `OrderDesk`:

items: `Consumer<Order> pipeline(List<String> auditLog, List<Order> processed)` returns one consumer that, for each order, first adds the line `"PROCESSED: <id> for <customer>"` to `auditLog`, then adds the order to `processed`.

`void processLarge(List<Order> orders, double threshold, Consumer<Order> pipeline)` feeds `pipeline` every order whose amount is **above** `threshold`, one at a time in list order; an order that appears twice is fed twice.

blocks.text: With orders `O1` (150.0, Alice), `O2` (75.0, Bob) and `O3` (200.0, Charlie) and a threshold of `100`:

rows: `["PROCESSED: O1 for Alice", "PROCESSED: O3 for Charlie"]`

blocks.text: The audit line for an order must already be written when that order is stored.

cases.says: Every order above the threshold is audited and stored, and the others are not.
andThen runs the first consumer first, so each order's audit line exists before the order is stored.
Only orders strictly above the threshold are processed; one exactly at it is not.
processLarge feeds the orders one at a time in list order, even for a long list; a parallel forEach scrambles the order.

concepts: A bound reference such as processed::add is a Consumer that stores every value into that one list.
Consumer.andThen hands each value to the first consumer and then to the second.
